linkedinPosts.content:
🚀 What the Last Few Weeks Looked Like for Me…

The last few weeks have honestly been a mix of learning, rebuilding fundamentals, and trying new things every single day.

As a part of the marquee batch at Parul University, I decided to restart my DSA journey with LeetCode once again. Sometimes growth is not about rushing ahead — it’s about going back to the basics and becoming stronger step by step.

Along with that, I also restarted MERN from the beginning, starting with simple HTML & CSS websites and gradually moving towards modern full-stack development.

And somewhere in between all this, I worked on a few really exciting things that I’ll hopefully share next month 👀

One of the biggest highlights was participating in the Odoo Hackathon, organized by Odoo and Parul University, and managed by the Technical Events Cell, Parul University.

Today was our first virtual round, where our problem statement was Travel Loop.
For the project, I developed the website using:
⚡ Next.js 16
⚛️ React 19
🛢️ Supabase for real-time database & authentication
🎨 Custom luxury-themed UI with Framer Motion animations

A huge thank you to my teammates Nipun Kulshrestha, Mahi Patel, and PRATVI HIMANSHU PATEL for all the support, teamwork, and effort during today’s hackathon round. Really grateful to be working with such amazing people 🤝

This journey keeps teaching me that consistency, teamwork, and strong fundamentals matter the most.
Still learning. Still building. 🚀

hashtag#BuildInPublic hashtag#OdooHackathon hashtag#LeetCode hashtag#DSA hashtag#MERNStack hashtag#NextJS hashtag#ReactJS hashtag#Supabase hashtag#WebDevelopment hashtag#StudentDeveloper hashtag#DeveloperJourney hashtag#Hackathon hashtag#CodingLife hashtag#LearningJourney

I wasn’t inactive.
I was building.

While my LinkedIn stayed quiet, my life didn’t.
The past few months have been intense — filled with learning, responsibilities, challenges, and moments that truly shaped me.

A major part of this journey was working on my Civic Issue Tracker project.
Not just building it — but pushing myself to think deeper:
Can this actually solve real problems? Can this create real impact?

At the same time, I stepped into a completely different role as an intern at the Technical Events Cell, Parul University.
Being part of organizing Tech Expo 2026 taught me what real execution looks like — coordination, pressure, teamwork… and delivering when it actually matters.

Then came exams — a phase of discipline and focus.

But growth didn’t stop there.

Right after, I was back again — building, improving, and pushing myself further.
Soon, I also got the opportunity to be part of organizing Design Hackathon 2026, adding another unforgettable experience to this journey.

And then… a moment that made everything feel worth it.

I was selected for India Innovates 2026 Hackathon,
and got the opportunity to represent my university Parul University at the national level at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

Standing there…
I realized — this is why I kept going, even when no one was watching.

Looking back, these months were never about being silent…
they were about being focused.

And sometimes, growth asks for difficult decisions.

Yesterday, I made one.

I stepped down from my internship to focus completely on what’s next —
to build more, learn more, and chase something bigger.

This is just the beginning.
